title: Sourcing & Project Coordinator: Promotional Products — Remote, Full-Time Contractor
description:
South Sun Solutions is a branded merchandise company. We work with agencies, mission-driven brands, and corporate clients, and our positioning is simple: we translate moments, ideas, and initiatives into gifts that last. Most of our industry is catalog-and-logo. Our value is in creative origination, product judgment, and anticipating the details before they become problems so people get items they keep. Sometimes that means designing something from scratch. Sometimes it means finding the right elevated object. And sometimes a client simply needs hats — done right, on time.



Sustainability, for us, means product longevity and material intentionality, not greenwashing. With that in mind, we’re also offering tech-enabled products that connect keepsake physical pieces with lasting digital experiences.



We’re a small team: two co-founders, plus a Strategic Account Manager (SAM) based in the Philippines. This role works directly with the SAM. It’s a full-time, long-term contractor role for someone who already knows the promotional products industry from the distributor side and wants to grow within a company that takes the work seriously and believes in consistency over intensity: some weeks have a heavier workload, some weeks are lighter; the goal is steady, high-quality execution over time, not constant urgency.



-----------------------------------



*What you’ll do*



In your first three months, your work centers on research, sourcing, and keeping our systems accurate and up to date.



~Product research and sourcing support~



• Research and recommend products against project requirements, with a focus on proactive projects and longer lead times

• Communicate with vendors on availability, pricing, and specs to prepare preliminary quotes

• Verify vendor payment details by phone before new or changed banking information is used — a standard fraud-prevention step we take whenever the timeline allows

• Keep ClickUp current so we have a truly robust project management system. This includes, but isn’t limited to: uploading all mockups to each project, linking
 threads to their corresponding projects, updating all quick-look fields, and maintaining the AR tracker (we plan to dedicate a knowledge transfer day to ClickUp during the onboarding phase)

• Set up the sync agenda doc for each call from our template — new doc, correct dates, labeled with the two-week span — at least a week ahead so everyone can add items as they come up

• Final product selection and project direction stay with the SAM. Rush projects stay with the SAM during this period.

• Other miscellaneous (but work-related) research and projects as they come up (for example: looking into freight forwarders, comparing options, and making recommendations)



~Client research~



• Research clients and prospects from lists we provide, using LinkedIn, Google, our database, and whatever else works: upcoming events, programs, past purchases, and where a merch opportunity could exist (get creative!)

• Add to the prospect list when you spot a good opportunity

• Gather and organize what you find early enough for us to act on it — ideally, the team knows about upcoming events three or more months out, when possible



~Product library and trend research~



• Review vendor product suggestions (these typically arrive by
) and organize the products that look like a good fit for our clients into product libraries by category (apparel, hard goods, etc.)

• Separately, maintain running lists of new and trending products. These can come from supplier sites, trade show recaps, industry news, or anything else that catches your eye



~Content and creative support~



• Build and maintain a bank of ready-to-post LinkedIn assets showcasing completed projects, so there’s always something to pull from. This is an ongoing responsibility, not something you wait to be assigned. The SAM directs this work and is the first point of contact for any questions; if you need further context on a project or the client, the Executive Creative Director is your resource

• Create visual templates and simple social graphics in Canva

• Contribute content ideas and support initiatives that help people see our work



-----------------------------------



*What you won’t own*



We value transparency, so clear role definitions matter to us. The SAM owns final client communication, product selection, pricing and margin decisions, quote approval, project prioritization, major vendor decisions, and anything that requires judgment about the overall client relationship.



As Sourcing & Project Coordinator, you work alongside the SAM. When the SAM requests support with live client work, that comes first; the rest of your time goes to ongoing, mostly self-directed work like building product libraries and researching prospects. Your research, sourcing, and organization make the team’s work stronger and directly support the growth of the business.



-----------------------------------



*Where we see this role going*



After three months, if we both want to move forward together, the role expands:



• Supporting all project types, including rush and time-sensitive work

• Responding to new inquiries and gathering initial project details (quantity, budget, timeline, product direction) before handing off to the SAM

• Flagging missing information, deadline risks, opportunities, and more before they become problems or we're too close to an event to pitch a client or prospect

• Building client-ready decks once product selection and direction are finalized

• Supporting concept-first outreach to target agencies and past clients

• Keeping our living documents current, especially upcoming client projects and events



Compensation grows with the role. The path we’re building toward is Coordinator → Senior Coordinator → Strategic Account Manager: growing into a second SAM role as the business grows.



-----------------------------------



*Who you’ll work with*



You’ll take day-to-day direction from our SAM. He sets your priorities, reviews your work, and is your first stop for questions about projects.



Our Executive Creative Director handles the personnel side: your onboarding, compensation, regular check-ins, and your 90-day evaluation. If something isn’t working — with your workload, how you’re being supported, or the working relationship itself — you can go to her directly.



You’ll join the company sync call every other week, and during your first 90 days you’ll have 1:1 check-ins with the Executive Creative Director on the weeks when there isn’t a sync call.



-----------------------------------



*What we’re looking for*



~Required~



• At least one year of experience at a promotional products distributor

• Working familiarity with Sage or ESP/ASI

• Experience with supplier portals (SanMar, alphabroder, or similar)

• Experience with a project management tool, and willingness to learn ClickUp

• Clear, professional English, spoken and written

• Comfortable working with direction, and comfortable working without it when the task calls for it — prospect research and product libraries are largely self-directed

• Available full-time during US Eastern business hours (roughly 9pm–6am Philippine time)



~A plus~



• Canva, Adobe, or other graphic design experience

• LinkedIn research experience

• University degree



~And the things that matter more than any tool~



Our clients expect higher-end pieces, and the question we start from isn’t “what do we put a logo on?”

but “what object makes sense for this moment?”



• You’re curious about who’s receiving the item and why. You’ll research the brand and the event before suggesting what the object should be.

• You have an eye for quality. You can tell a basic item from an elevated one, and a “good-enough” item from the right one — and you’ll keep looking/reaching out until you find the vendor(s) who can make the

elevated version.

• You notice what others miss — a material that’s off, a lead time that doesn't actually work, a detail the client would catch (and you catch it before the client does!).

• You’re reliable. When you take on a responsibility, no matter how small the task, it gets done.

• You make educated guesses where possible (we love to foster creative, independent thinking), and you ask when you’re unsure — there is no stupid question.

• You’re looking for a long-term role with growth, not a gig.



-----------------------------------



*Working structure and compensation*



• Full-time contractor role, 40 hours per week, fully remote

• US Eastern business hours

• $600–$800 USD per month, with a defined ramp over the first 90 days based on milestones our ECD will suggest, and we'll agree upon together

• A formal evaluation at 90 days, where we both d
 whether to move forward together

• Compensation continues to grow with expanded responsibility and performance as the business grows



-----------------------------------



*How we work*



Five principles shape everything we do, including how we treat the people we work with:



• People over profit, while staying profitable

• Structure that serves everyone, not just the business

• Consistency over intensity

• Accountability as normal, not as punishment

• People as partners, not resources



If this sounds like how you want to work, please follow the directions below to apply.  



-----------------------------------



*How to apply*



Please start your application with the word LONGEVITY so we know you’ve read the full posting.



Then include:



1. A short introduction (3–5 sentences)

2. Why this role interests you

3. One sourcing request you handled: what the client asked for, what you recommended, and what you’d do differently now, if anything

4. Two suppliers you’ve worked with regularly, and one thing you learned about each (lead times, quality, service — whatever stood out)

5. One process, system, or responsibility you fully owned, not assisted with

6. Confirmation that you can work US Eastern business hours full-time



-----------------------------------



*What happens next*



We’ll review applications through September 19 and schedule first interviews the following week.

Depending on how those go, we may invite a small number of candidates to a second conversation

and/or a short paid sourcing exercise. Target start date is early-to-mid October, knowing we may need

to work around a notice period.



We look forward to hearing from you!

title: AI Video Editor
description:
AI VIDEO EDITOR - SHORT VERTICAL REELS, ONGOING WORK



Rate: $10 per finished reel, flat

Schedule: Async. No fixed hours, no time tracker, no meetings.

Volume: Ongoing, every month





WHY YOU MIGHT LIKE THIS ONE



The brief is already done. You get the full script, the voiceover direction, a shot list with timecodes, the exact words that appear on screen, the fonts, the hex colors, and a storyboard with every frame drawn out. No client calls. No guessing what someone wants. No three rounds of "can you make it pop."



You work on your own schedule, you talk directly to me, and you get paid on delivery of each reel.





ABOUT US



Boost Web Studio is a small US marketing studio. We help local service businesses with their Google Business Profile, website, and social content. These reels explain simple marketing ideas to business owners who are not marketers, so they stay clear and friendly rather than flashy.





WHAT YOU DELIVER



One vertical reel under 30 seconds, 9:16, as a finished MP4.



A typical reel has an animated phone screen, text appearing one item at a time, an AI voiceover, full-sentence captions, and a clean end card.





REVISIONS



One round, for small things we d
 to add or change after seeing it.



Things that do not match the brief are not revisions and do not count against you as extra work. We just fix them before the reel is done. Wrong font, wrong color, a misspelled business name, a number that changes between shots, a screen that contradicts the voiceover.





WHAT WE LOOK FOR



- You animate interfaces, not just cut clips. After Effects or equivalent.

- You are comfortable with AI tools for images, voiceover, and video, and you know when hand-built is faster and cleaner than generated.

- You are careful with type. A font, a hex code, and a safe zone land right the first time.

- You read written briefs in English and reply clearly.





WHAT WE CARE ABOUT MOST



Text that is real and readable. No garbled AI lettering, no placeholder text, no business name that changes spelling halfway through.





TWO WAYS TO APPLY



Just send your portfolio. Three vertical short-form videos you edited yourself. That is a complete application and it gets a real look.



Or send the reel too. The full brief for our next reel is below. Build it, watermark it, send it. It puts you ahead of portfolio-only applicants because I can see exactly how you handle our format. If I pick you, I pay the $10 straight away, you send the clean file, and that becomes our first reel together.



THE BRIEF - 25-SECOND REEL



9:16, 1080 x 1920, 30fps. MP4. Figtree. Navy #00388F, cyan #00B5E2.



Voiceover: natural American woman's voice, warm and conversational.



SCRIPT



Somebody near you needs a plumber right now.

They grab their phone and search.

Google shows them three. You're the third one.

Fewer reviews than the two above you, and your listing's still mostly blank.

No hours. No services. No photos.

You can fill all that in yourself, and it doesn't cost anything.

Want a hand with it? Get a free Google checkup.



SHOT LIST



0-4s. Open on movement. Someone holding a phone near a leaking water heater. "plumber near me" types in.



4-8s. Three results load. Scroll slightly until Cedar Creek Plumbing appears third.



8-12s. Slight zoom. Outline the whole Cedar Creek listing in cyan. No label, no arrow.



12-16s. Open the Cedar Creek profile. Hours missing, Services missing, Recent photos missing, one at a time.



16-21s. Fill each in, with a small cyan checkmark as it completes:

Open - Closes 5 PM / Drain Cleaning - Pipe Repair - Water Heaters / three recent plumbing photos.



21-25s. Cyan end card: "See what your Google profile is missing." / GET FREE GOOGLE CHECKUP / small white Boost Web Studio logo near the bottom.



KEEP CONSISTENT THROUGHOUT



Ridgeline Plumbing 4.9 (287), Oakfield Plumbing 4.7 (164), Cedar Creek Plumbing 4.2 (28). Cedar Creek's numbers never change. Do not show hours while the voiceover says the hours are missing.



Captions in full sentences, inside the Instagram and
 safe zones.



Send us a message and we will send you the storyboard and the assets for the sample reel.Recreate the search and profile screens however works best for you.





HOW TO APPLY



Keep it short. I read every application that includes these.



1. Three vertical videos you edited yourself. Links, not attachments. For one of them, tell me which parts were AI-generated and which you built by hand.

2. Which AI tools you use and what you use each one for.

3. How long a 25-second reel takes you from brief to first draft.

4. That the flat $10 per reel works for you.

5. The reel, watermarked, if you d
 to build it.

6. Start your message with CEDAR so I know this post got read.



I reply to everyone who follows those six points.

title: Experienced Amazon FBA Online Arbitrage Sourcing VA
description:
We are looking for an experienced Amazon FBA Online Arbitrage Product Sourcing VA. This is not an entry-level position. You should already understand Amazon FBA sourcing and be able to find profitable leads independently.



Your primary responsibility will be sourcing profitable online-arbitrage products that meet our buying criteria.



You must have hands-on experience with SellerAmp SAS and Keepa and understand how to properly analyze a potential lead before submitting it.



Responsibilities include:



Online arbitrage product sourcing

Manual sourcing

Storefront stalking and reverse sourcing

Finding and analyzing profitable product leads

Using SellerAmp SAS to evaluate ROI, profit, fees, eligibility, competition, and other key metrics

Reading Keepa charts and understanding sales rank, price history, Buy Box behavior, offer count, Amazon presence, and historical trends

Checking variations and identifying the correct ASIN/product match

Evaluating seller competition and whether a product is realistically worth purchasing

Finding discounts, coupons, promo codes, and cashback opportunities when applicable

Recording qualified leads accurately in our sourcing sheet

Following our minimum profit, ROI, sales-rank, competition, and other sourcing requirements



Requirements:

Previous Amazon FBA online-arbitrage sourcing experience is required. You should already know SellerAmp SAS, Keepa, storefront stalking/reverse sourcing, and manual sourcing. You should be able to explain your sourcing process and demonstrate that you can distinguish a genuinely good lead from a product that only looks profitable at first glance.



When applying, please include your Amazon FBA sourcing experience, how long you have used SellerAmp and Keepa, the sourcing methods you normally use, how many qualified leads you can typically produce per day, your availability, and your expected hourly rate.



Desired hours: I’d start around 15–20 hours/week, then increase hours if their leads consistently convert into profitable buys.



For the title, I’d definitely include “Online Arbitrage”. “Amazon FBA VA” alone will attract a lot of applicants with listing, customer-service, or general Seller Central experience rather than actual sourcing experience.

 communication, landing pages, and an organized follow up plan.

title: Vendor sourcing specialist (USA)
description:
Vendor Sourcing Specialist (USA)



Task: Beverage Co-Packer Outreach & Research 



Summary



I’m launching a premium sparkling functional beverage (clean caffeine + L-theanine + electrolytes, 12oz can) and need someone to call/contact a list of beverage manufacturers and co-packers, ask a defined set of questions, and log the answers in a shared tracker. Some companies have already been contacted by
 — this role is about getting the missing information by phone (or follow-up
 if a call isn’t possible), plus doing first-touch outreach to a second list of manufacturers we haven’t contacted yet.

This is not a sales or persuasion role. You’re gathering factual information: capabilities, pricing, minimums, samples, and compliance documentation. Most of the companies are in CA and need to be contacted between 9am - 5pm PST, so please only apply if the time difference is not a problem.



Structure: Paid Trial, Then Full Job



Phase 1 (trial, paid separately): Call the 5 priority companies flagged below, get complete answers, log them in the tracker in the

format specified. I’ll review the quality before assigning the rest.



Phase 2 (if trial goes well): Full remaining list — both follow-up calls and new outreach.



Priority 5 for Phase 1

These are the highest-leverage first calls — a mix of fastest-path-to-sample and one-stop shops that could shortcut needing separate formulation + canning partners:



1. LTBB (Lucky To Be Beverage) — has ready, market-tested stock formulas; fastest path to an actual sample, no formulation wait.

2. MacroCap Labs — vertically integrated (formulation + canning + fulfillment in one facility); could solve the “nobody wants to

formulate” problem in a single vendor.

3. Big Brands — turnkey formulation + co-packing specifically for functional/adaptogen beverages; another one-stop candidate.

4. BevZero — full turnkey concept-to-product, 30+ years in the category; broad, established option.

5. Chapter Foods — not a manufacturer, a matchmaking/consulting service. Worth calling early since a good conversation here could surface better-fit co-packers than cold
ing the rest of the list one by one.



What You’re Calling About

A premium sparkling clean-energy + hydration beverage. Manufacturer-facing context, if asked:

12 oz aluminum can

~40–60mg caffeine (prefer clean/natural source like green tea), L-theanine, electrolytes

Zero/very low added sugar, low calorie

Exploring both private-label (their existing stock formula) and semi-custom routes

Two flavors/SKUs planned for initial launch

Early-stage: want a first sample round before committing to volume



Once Stephanie identifies the company, the first ask on that call is to get the

specific contact’s name and direct phone number, same as every other entry.

Information to Get on Every Call



1. Private label or custom only? Do they have existing stock formulas we can taste/sample, or is everything custom-built?

2. MOQ — per SKU, in cans/cases, for both stock and custom (if different)

3. Pricing — indicative per-can cost at initial volume and at scale; any setup/tooling fees

4. Samples — can they send samples, cost (if any), and turnaround time

5. Lead time — production and reorder lead times

6. Formula ownership/exclusivity terms — do we own the formula, or is it licensed/shared

7. Compliance documents (get copies or confirmation these exist):

GFSI audit certificate (SQF Level 2/3, BRCGS, or FSSC 22000)

FDA facility registration number

Product-specific HACCP plan

Most recent third-party food safety audit report (e.g. Silliker, Eurofins, NSF)

8. Warehousing / direct-to-distributor capability — can they ship direct to distributors or do we need our own 3PL



How to Log Results

Update the shared tracker (MVM Manufacturer Tracker) after every call — don’t batch it. (To be provided)

For each company, fill in: 

- Status/Latest Action (date + what was discussed)

 - MOQ - Pricing/Financial Notes

 - Capability/Fit Analysis (your read on whether they’re a real fit) 

- The four compliance columns (mark received/confirmed/not available)

I*f a call goes to voi
 or gets no answer, log the attempt and try again — don’t mark it “no response” after one try.



Notes

Be upfront that this is an early-stage brand exploring options, not placing an order yet — don’t overpromise volume.

If a company says they don’t do private label or the MOQ is clearly incompatible (e.g. 100,000+ units for a first pilot), don’t spend time pushing — log it as disqualified and move on.

Questions during the trial phase: reach out before guessing.

title: Executive Assistant & Lead Generation Specialist
description:
About the Role



We are a growing alcohol and beverage business looking for a highly organised and proactive Executive Assistant & Lead Generation Specialist to support the founder. This is a broad support role combining lead generation, sales outreach, CRM management, follow-up, research, data entry, and executive assistance.



The ideal candidate will become an extension of the founder over time — helping organise opportunities, keep prospective customers moving through the pipeline, identify new hospitality and retail prospects, and take recurring administrative work off the founder's plate. The role will initially be part-time, with the potential to increase in hours as the candidate becomes more familiar with the business and takes on additional responsibilities.



Work Structure & Requirements



Location: Remote / Virtual

Schedule: Part-time (10 hours per week)

Time Zone: EST business hours

Compensation: $7 USD per hour



Key Responsibilities



1. Lead Generation & Prospect Research



Research and identify relevant hospitality groups, restaurant groups, bars, distributors, retailers, and other potential customers

Identify the appropriate decision-makers and stakeholders within target organisations

Build accurate prospect lists containing names, job titles,
 addresses, phone numbers, and company information

Research the largest and most relevant operators within target markets

Maintain organised prospect databases and continuously identify new sales opportunities



2. Sales Outreach & Follow-Up



Conduct outbound
 outreach to prospective customers using messaging and positioning provided by the founder

Manage ongoing follow-up sequences and ensure opportunities do not fall through the cracks

Follow up consistently with prospects who have expressed interest or require additional information

Help turn business cards, introductions, referrals, and existing contacts into organised sales opportunities

Escalate warm or qualified opportunities to the founder when appropriate

Maintain detailed notes on conversations, next steps, and follow-up dates



3. CRM & Pipeline Management



Enter and organise leads within the company CRM or sales tracking system

Keep contact information, opportunity stages, notes, and follow-up activities accurate and up to date

Track outstanding actions across prospective customers and partnerships

Create simple reports or summaries of outreach activity, responses, and opportunities

Help establish stronger processes for organising the company's growing sales pipeline



4. Executive & Administrative Support



Provide day-to-day administrative support to the founder

Organise information, documents, contacts, and outstanding tasks

Assist with follow-ups arising from meetings, events, networking, and customer conversations

Help document recurring processes and gradually take ownership of repeatable administrative tasks

Support ad hoc research and operational projects as required



5. Data Entry & Compliance Administration



Assist with recurring data-entry and administrative requirements across different state or government systems

Enter information into relevant portals accurately and according to documented processes

Learn recurring workflows directly from the founder through recorded or live training sessions

Document processes and create simple SOPs so tasks can be completed independently in future

Double-check calculations and information before submission and obtain approval where required

Maintain accurate records of completed submissions and outstanding requirements



Required Skills & Experience



Experience: 3+ years in Executive Assistance, Lead Generation, Sales Support, Business Development Support, or a similar role

Industry: Previous experience within alcohol, beverages, CPG, hospitality, food & beverage, or a related industry is strongly preferred

Lead Generation: Strong lead-generation and online research capabilities; experience identifying decision-makers and sourcing accurate contact information

Outreach: Comfortable conducting professional cold
 outreach and persistent follow-up

title: Junior Video Editor
description:
Basic Headline Video Editor

Exchange Life · Fully Remote · Full-Time Contractor · ~40 hrs/week $5 USD/hour to $10 USD/hour + $300–$800/month in performance bonuses

About Exchange Life

Exchange Life is a fast-growing e-commerce travel jewelry brand. We sell collectible country charms for travelers, with new product lines launching soon. Our content team of editors, filmmakers, and creators works fully remotely across the world.

This role is a starting point, and we're straight about that — it's focused work editing headline videos to a proven format. But it's a starting point on a team that promotes from the inside. Many of our editors have been with us two or more years, and the ones who started here are now the people briefing everyone else.

Where You'll Be in Six Months

AI Advanced Editor.

That's the next title, and it's the step most of our strong headline editors make inside their first six months. An AI Advanced Editor works on our highest-leverage creative: AI-assisted video, hook development, and the ad formats we scale behind. You stop working purely to a template and start building the ones other people follow.

It's d
 by performance, not tenure. Produce winners consistently and you'll get there sooner.

What You'll Earn

Base: $5 USD/hour

Performance bonuses: $300–$800/month, paid per winning creative — when a video you cut hits our performance thresholds or scales on paid, you get paid for it

There's no cap on how good your month can be

What Success Looks Like

Within three to six months, you're consistently producing headline videos that perform on both paid and organic channels — 50%+ thumb-stop rates and 30%+ hold rates — and iterating on winning formats without needing day-to-day direction.

Responsibilities

Edit TikTok and Reels headline content optimized for hook rate, retention, and watch time

Review past edits daily, identify what is and isn't working, and apply those lessons

Work with the marketing team to test new creative angles and iterate on proven formats

Turn work around quickly and communicate proactively each day

Track TikTok and Instagram trends and apply them where relevant

Requirements

A recent portfolio of short-form edits (ideally 20+ from the past few months)

Ability to break down why a viral video or high-performing ad worked

Comfortable reading performance metrics (hook rate, retention, watch time) and adjusting accordingly

Skilled in CapCut Pro or a comparable editing tool

Strong written and spoken English, and the ability to work independently

Takes ownership and applies feedback consistently

Preferred

Experience editing for e-commerce brands

Exposure to AI video tools, talking heads, or voiceover formats

Experience interpreting paid ad metrics

What You'll Learn Here

Most editing roles teach you software. This one teaches you why things sell. You'll get direct access to paid ad data on real spend, see which of your creatives print money and which die, and build the one skill that makes editors expensive: knowing what to make before you make it.

Access to courses and paid software

1-on-1 mentorship from our Content Lead

Full visibility into TikTok and Meta performance data on your own work

Not a Fit If

Your portfolio is mostly long-form, YouTube, or event/wedding content

You prefer a fixed schedule or close day-to-day supervision

You're looking for a short-term project or side gig

Working Style

Independent contractor engagement, paid in USD

100% remote, approximately 40 hours per week, long-term

Flexible schedule with no required timezone overlap — async communication daily

Flexible paid time off, coordinated with the team

Tools: CapCut Pro (or comparable), TikTok and Meta analytics

No micromanagement

How to Apply

Applications take about five minutes. We review every submission.



APPLY HERE:

title: Social Media & Content Manager
description:
About the Role



We are an emerging beverage brand inspired by Ayurveda — the 5,000-year-old Indian wellness practice centered around daily rituals for a more holistic and balanced life. Currently growing our retail presence in New York City alongside our e-commerce business, we are entering an exciting stage of growth with additional product launches planned and a strong focus on building community and brand awareness across the U.S.



We're looking for a Social Media & Content Manager who can help co-lead our social media strategy while also being highly hands-on with day-to-day execution. This is not simply a scheduling or community management position — we want someone who brings ideas to the table, helps establish a clear content strategy, identifies what is and isn't working, and works closely with the founders to bring that strategy to life.



Work Structure & Requirements



Location: Remote / Virtual

Schedule: Part-time (20 hours per week)

Time Zone: EST business hours

Compensation: $8 USD per hour



Key Responsibilities



1. Social Media Strategy



Develop and help lead the organic social media strategy across Instagram and TikTok

Establish clear content pillars, formats, themes, and posting strategies rather than creating content on an ad-hoc basis

Help grow our presence and reach specifically within the U.S. market, with an initial focus on New York and relevant U.S. consumer communities

Identify opportunities to improve audience targeting and ensure content reaches the brand's intended demographic

Develop platform-specific strategies for Instagram and TikTok while identifying opportunities to repurpose high-performing content across channels

Build content plans around new product launches, retail growth, founder stories, and other key brand moments



2. Content Creation & Video Editing



Work closely with the founders to develop content ideas, scripts, hooks, and creative briefs for founder-led videos

Give the founders clear direction on what content should be filmed and how it should be structured

Edit founder-shot footage into engaging TikToks, Instagram Reels, and Stories

Create strong opening hooks, pacing, captions, and edits designed to maximize retention and engagement

Identify relevant TikTok, Instagram, and broader cultural trends and adapt them creatively for the brand

Help maintain a consistent brand voice, look, and feel across all social content

Develop organic content and creative concepts that can also be tested and repurposed as paid social advertising creatives



3. Publishing & Community Management



Own or support the day-to-day publishing of content across Instagram and TikTok

Manage comments, DMs, and general community engagement

Proactively engage with relevant U.S.-based consumers, creators, communities, and complementary brands

Help build genuine relationships around the brand rather than relying solely on paid audience acquisition

Identify relevant local communities, events, wellness groups, creators, and other opportunities that could strengthen our presence in New York and the wider U.S. market



4. Creator & UGC Support



Identify creators and UGC opportunities that align with our target customer and brand positioning

Coordinate basic creator outreach, product seeding, and UGC collaborations

Maintain creator lists and help manage communication and follow-ups

Identify high-performing creator content that could be repurposed across organic and paid channels



Required Skills & Experience



Experience: 3+ years in social media management, social strategy, content marketing, or a similar role

Platforms: Strong experience managing and growing brands across Instagram and TikTok

Strategy: Demonstrated ability to develop social media strategy as well as execute it

Video: Strong short-form video editing skills, particularly for TikTok and Instagram Reels; excellent understanding of hooks, storytelling, retention, and short-form content best practices

Trends: Ability to identify trends and translate them into content that feels relevant to a specific brand rather than simply copying trends

Communication: Strong written English; ability to write engaging social copy, captions, scripts, and content concepts

Analytics: Comfortable analyzing social media performance and making recommendations based on data

Profile: Highly proactive, creative, and comfortable suggesting ideas rather than waiting for detailed instructions; sits somewhere between a Social Media Strategist, Content Manager, and hands-on Creator



To Apply:

Kindly send your resume, portfolio and introduction video

title: Job Title: Inbound Sales Closer & VA (GoHighLevel & Mapping Experience)
description:
We are seeking high-performing Inbound Sales Closers to handle inbound calls and web inquiries for our fast-paced Christmas light installation business. You will manage full-funnel phone sales: warmly greeting leads, pre-screening project budgets, building live custom design mockups using mapping software, and closing jobs on the first call.



Schedule: Coverage needed 12 hours/day, 7 days/week (multiple shifts available).



Pay: $6.00/hour base + uncapped sales performance bonuses.



Key Responsibilities:



-Lead Handling: Answer incoming phone calls and follow up immediately with newly submitted web inquiries.

-Sales & Pitching: Deliver a natural, engaging introduction to explain our full-service offering without reading off a rigid script.

-Budget Screening: Pre-screen potential clients by establishing our $700 minimum project starting price early in the call.

-Live Custom Mockups: Locate property photos via Google Maps and Zillow to generate live design mockups while on the line with the customer.

-Closing Deals: Walk clients through their customized proposals, address objections, and secure deposits on the spot.

-Pipeline Management: Maintain and update contact records and deal stages inside GoHighLevel (GHL).



Requirements & Qualifications:



-Flawless Spoken English: Native or near-native English fluency with zero to minimal accent to ensure effortless, high-trust communication with US homeowners.

-Sales Competency: Confident handling price objections, guiding conversations, and directly asking for the sale.

-US Home Familiarity: Ability to visually identify standard American home architectural features (e.g., rooflines, dormers, peaks, gutters) from photos.

-Software Proficiency: Familiarity with GoHighLevel (GHL) and navigation of Google Maps/Zillow (design/mapping tool experience is a major plus; training provided).

-Home Office Setup: High-speed internet connection, quiet dedicated environment, and a noise-canceling headset.



How to Apply (Mandatory Instructions)

To be considered for this position, please submit:



1. Your Resume

2. Weekly Availability: State your preferred working hours and available days per week (e.g., 5 days/week, weekends, M-F).

3. 1-2 Minute Audio Audition: Submit a recording (via Vocaroo or Google Drive link) performing the roleplay script below.



Note: Applications submitted without a voice recording will be automatically disqualified.



[Roleplay Audition Script]

Read the script below as the VA. We are evaluating tone, clarity, pacing, and conversational flow—do NOT read like a robot!



VA: "Thanks for calling Fresh Christmas Lights, how can we brighten up your day?"   

(Pause 2 seconds | imagine customer says: "Hi, I saw your yard sign down the street and wanted to get a quote for Christmas lights on my house.")   



VA: "Great! We’d love to help light up your house. We put lights on thousands of homes every year, so you’re in great hands! Do you mind if I share a quick outline of how our service works so we can see if we're a good fit?"   



(Pause 2 seconds | imagine customer says: "Sure, go ahead.")   



VA: "Awesome! We’re a full service Christmas light company. That means we custom fit the lights directly to your house by cutting wires and attaching custom plugs and bulbs. You won't have any messy cords hanging down—it looks extremely clean and professional.   



We also provide automated timers set to your schedule, and all high quality materials are included under our light leasing program, so you never have to buy or store the lights yourself. That means full maintenance is included free of charge—if a bulb or plug ever goes out, you just call us and we come fix it at zero extra charge.   



Then in January, we reach out, take all the lights down, and store them safely in our warehouse for next season. Plus, while we're out there, we offer discounts on our other business services like gutter cleaning! How does all that sound?"   



(Pause 2 seconds | imagine customer says: "That sounds really great.")   



VA: "Wonderful! Our custom projects start at $700 and go up from there depending on the home size and design complexity. If that's within your starting budget, I’d love to take down your address right now and pull up a live picture of your house with lights on it in just a couple of minutes!"

title: Executive Assistant to Founder (Remote, PH-Based, PST Hours)
description:
Umbrella Property Services is a building services company based in Vancouver. We’re on a mission to attract, develop, and empower people from around the world to become better leaders.



I’m Ryan, the Founder, and I move fast. I think in ideas and loose ends. Your job is to turn those into clear plans, tight calendars, and closed loops. You report directly to me and act as the primary leverage point for my time and attention.



This is not a basic VA role. I’m looking for a true Executive Assistant who creates structure around me. Someone who wants to become exceptional at executive support, systems, prioritization, and follow-through over the foreseeable future. This role is not intended to be a short-term stepping stone while you immediately pursue a different career or business.



About Ryan & How We Work

- I’m not a micromanager. I’m not looking over your shoulder or nitpicking details. My style is “good enough, ship it, keep moving.”

- I’m chaotic by nature: lots of ideas, lots of moving pieces, and I’d rather be doing deals, strategy, and sales than admin.



Your job is to:

- Put just enough structure around me so my days are sane,

- Protect my calendar so I have real focus time,

- Own the admin and follow-through so I don’t have to chase you or the work.



If you like bringing order to a fast-moving founder and being trusted to run with things, you’ll fit here.



Your Core Outcome

- Give me back time, focus, and mental space.

- When I hand you something, you own it until it’s done. I should not have to chase updates, remember details, or manage follow-through. If you need clarity, you ask. If you don’t, you just get it done.



What Success Looks Like in the First 60 Days

- You fully own my calendar: no double bookings, protected focus time, realistic days.

- My inbox is consistently triaged; I only see what actually needs my brain, with drafts ready where appropriate.

- Recurring admin and follow‑ups are handled without me chasing you, and I’m spending noticeably more time on sales, strategy, and deals.



What You’ll Own

1. Calendar & Communication

- Protect and manage my calendar; no double bookings, clear buffers, realistic days.

- Triage inbox and messages; draft replies and summarize what needs my decision.

- Ensure follow-ups and responses don’t fall through the cracks.

2. Follow-Up & Accountability

- Capture commitments from meetings and conversations.

- Turn discussions into clear next actions with owners and deadlines.

- Follow up with internal and external stakeholders and push (respectfully) when things stall.

3. Problem Solving

- Bring solutions, not just problems.

- When something blocks you, come back with: “Here’s what happened, here are options, here’s what I recommend.”

- Ask smart clarifying questions instead of waiting passively.

4. Projects & Operations

- Coordinate small projects and initiatives. This is light operational coordination, not a general operations manager role.

- Prepare agendas, documents, and materials for meetings.

- Maintain simple systems for tasks, SOPs, and follow-ups.

- Improve or automate repetitive admin where possible, including with AI tools.

- Handle personal admin (bookings, reservations, personal tasks) so I can stay focused on high‑value work.



You’ll Succeed Here If You Are

- Highly proactive and self-directed; you don’t wait to be told what to do next.

- Strong at follow-through and holding others accountable.

- Comfortable “managing up” to a busy, idea-driven founder.

- Clear, concise written communicator.

- Calm when priorities change and things are a bit chaotic.

- Detail-oriented and reliable; you take pride in clean work.

- Comfortable working with ambiguity and turning it into structure.

- AI-literate and hungry to keep learning.



This Role Is Not For You If

- You need step-by-step instructions for every task.

- You get stressed by someone who moves fast and changes priorities.

- You wait to be chased for updates instead of closing the loop yourself.



Non-Negotiables (Read Carefully)

- Based in the Philippines and able to work 7:30 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. PST, Monday–Friday (40 hrs/week).

- Minimum 2 years supporting a founder / CEO / executive as an EA, PA, or similar role.

- Excellent written and spoken English.

- Comfortable using Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets) and Slack for daily communication.

If you do not meet the above, your application will not be considered.



Compensation & Setup

- 30 days paid time off per year, aligned with the Canadian calendar (not PH public holidays).

- Bonus opportunities after 3 months, based on reliability, quality, and ownership.

How to Apply

description:
We're looking for a part-time, long-term setter to join our team.



We run a fast-growing AI education/personal brand and have people booking strategy calls every day. Your job is to personally follow up with every lead, build rapport, qualify them, answer basic questions, and make sure they actually show up for their scheduled call.



Our goal is simple: increase show rates and make sure our calendar is filled with qualified people who are serious about attending.



Responsibilities

Message every new booked lead immediately after they schedule.

Build genuine conversations through iMessage.

Qualify leads and answer basic questions.

Follow up before their scheduled call.

Confirm attendance and reduce no-shows.

Reschedule leads when appropriate.

Keep detailed notes on each conversation.

Work closely with our sales team.

Requirements

Excellent written English.

Friendly, personable, and confident communicator.

Strong sales or appointment-setting experience is preferred.

Highly organized and responsive.

Comfortable talking with people throughout the day.

Reliable internet connection.

Available during U.S. business hours.

Apple Device Requirement



This position requires you to own at least one Apple device (MacBook, iPhone, or iPad).



We use iMessage to communicate with our leads. We will provide a dedicated business Apple account and business phone number for work purposes. You will sign into our work account on your Apple device and use it only for communicating with leads.



Compensation

$2.5/hour

Long-term opportunity with room to grow



If you apply, please include:



Your location.

Your English proficiency.

Any appointment setting or sales experience.

Whether you own a MacBook, iPhone, or iPad (please specify which device).

Your availability in U.S. time zones.

Why you'd be a great fit for this role.

title: Project Manager/Operations Manager
description:
What Winning Looks Like



Every active project has one owner, a WBS, a schedule, and a status in ClickUp that matches reality.

No critical component is ever coin-flipped: crew confirmed with a backup day, gear planned, vendors tracked with proof of progress weeks out.

The team runs on the system — Connect Team, EOD reports, ClickUp, SOP-first — and the SOPs move from "In review" to "Validated."

Deliverables ship on time at the counts sold, and every one has cleared the QC tracker before the client sees it.

The founder gets one weekly view: what shipped, what is at risk, and your recommendation — never a pile of problems.

Nothing operational routes to the founder by default.



Your First 30 Days



Days 1–7 — Extraction & Baseline. Interview the founder and every team lead. Audit every active project: WBS against ClickUp, crew and gear status, open client items, critical components at risk. Read the playbook and every SOP, noting which are validated and which are not.



Days 8–14 — The Pipeline. Install the weekly pipeline review. Fix WBS-to-ClickUp drift. Put one owner and one date on every open item. Deliver a prioritized list of what is leaking time, money, or momentum.



Days 15–30 — The Operating Rhythm. Set the internal pre-production meeting cadence, the crew confirmation standard, and the vendor tracking standard. Validate the ten SOPs the team touches most. Present the founder the first weekly ops view and your 90-day plan.

Key Responsibilities





Pipeline: Own the production pipeline end to end. Confirmed events in within 24 hours. Every project staged, scoped, and scheduled before planning begins.



Pre-production: Run internal pre-production meetings. Shooting schedules from the client run of show. Equipment planning. Crew confirmed with a backup day. Call sheets out early.



Crew & vendors: Confirm, brief, and hold crew to the Production Policy. Track every vendor to the deadline with proof of progress. Invoiced hours match Connect Team.



Communication: Enforce the communication lines: up and then over, one owner per thing, client communication through the project lead. Model the three-channel, daily-until-received standard.



Quality & delivery: Own the video review tracker. Nothing ships without the QC pass. Revision rounds and scope creep handled as the changes they are.



Systems & SOPs: Own the operations manual. Turn recorded processes into SOPs, move SOPs to Validated, and retire the ones the team has outgrown.



People: Run training assignments and onboarding. Screen and coordinate hires. Process contractor payments on payday.



Reporting: One weekly operations view for the founder with insight and a recommendation.



What You Bring



5+ years running operations, production management, or project management in a production company, agency, events business, or other deadline-driven services company.

Proven ownership of a multi-project pipeline with remote crew and contractors.

Fluency in ClickUp or an equivalent PM system, and the discipline to keep it matching reality.

Vendor and crew management with a track record of catching problems weeks out, not days.

Clear, direct written and verbal communication; comfortable holding people to the standard.

Familiarity with video production is a strong advantage. You do not need to shoot or edit, but you need to understand what the editor needs from the shooter and what the client was promised.



Who You Are



You are an owner of outcomes, not a scheduler of tasks. You look people in the eye and tell them they are your bottleneck. You check in daily and it does not feel like nagging to you, because the alternative is a project quietly dying. You dig when something sounds too good, and you never take a vendor’s word for it. You can take a company that runs on the founder’s memory and make it run on a system.



How To Apply



Reply with your resume, a one-paragraph cover letter, and a Loom video (max 5 minutes) explaining why you are the right Operations Manager for RDM.

title: Automation Builder (AI-Assisted) – Make + GoHighLevel + ClickUp
description:
We're a fast-growing real estate and property management company that runs on automation. Our core tools are Make, GoHighLevel (GHL), and ClickUp, and we use AI tools (Claude, Claude Code) in everything we build.



We're hiring an Automation Builder. This is an execution role. We hand you written specs and short videos describing exactly what to build. You build it, test it, and turn it around fast. You are not designing our systems; our lead automation engineer does that. Your job is to take a clear spec and deliver a clean, working build, every time.



If you use AI tools daily and you're the kind of person who reads the spec twice and delivers exactly what was asked, this role was written for you.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build automations from written specs in Make (webhooks, filters, routers, field mapping)

Build workflows, pipelines, and automations in GoHighLevel from specs

Build and update ClickUp structures (lists, statuses, custom fields, templates) from specs

Use Claude and other AI tools to build faster; this is expected, not a nice-to-have

Test everything you build and fix what breaks

Write a short note documenting each build

Turn tickets around quickly and communicate clearly when something is blocked



YOU'D BE A GREAT FIT IF

You already use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) as part of how you build

You follow specs exactly and don't improvise unless asked

You have hands-on experience in Make, Zapier, or n8n

You understand webhooks, APIs, and JSON at a practical level

You test your own work before calling it done

You communicate clearly in English

GHL and ClickUp experience is a plus, not a requirement; we can teach the tools, we can't teach follow-through



ROLE DETAILS

Full-time, remote

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8 AM – 5 PM CST (includes lunch break)

Pay: $3–5 USD/hour, based on experience

Long-term role with growth potential



HOW TO APPLY

Message us here on OLJ with:

Your resume

A link to anything you've built: a Loom walkthrough, portfolio, or screenshots of real automations



That's it. Send us what you already have; you don't need to make anything new to apply.



OUR HIRING PROCESS (so you know what to expect)

We review your application, usually within 2 business days

Quick 10-minute video call with our lead automation engineer

A short paid sample task (about 30 minutes, $10)

Offer, starting with a 2-week paid trial on real work

title: Video Editor
description:
The One-Sentence Test



If the Lead Editor still has to open every timeline to know whether it is on time, on brand, and QC-clean, this role is not working. The right Video Editor owns the cut from selects to delivery so the Lead Editor can lead and the founder can direct.



The Mission



Turn raw event footage into finished deliverables that make the client look world-class and that their audience actually watches. You own recaps, full sessions, testimonials, and short-form reels from prep through 
 delivery, working inside RDM’s post-production SOPs in DaVinci Resolve. There are two scoreboards on every project: the client’s — delivered as promised, on time, at the counts agreed — and the audience’s — who stopped scrolling, how long they watched, how many finished. You are accountable to both.



What Winning Looks Like



Every deliverable ships inside its turnaround window, at the count that was sold.

Cuts clear internal QC on first submission, and the share of client approvals without a second revision round rises every quarter.

Every piece has a hook, a middle, and an ending you can defend, and at least one moment the client asks how we got.

Names, titles, and specs are right every time — verified against a source, never from memory.

Revisions come back with every note handled, and version history in 
 stays clean.

You know how each piece performed out of ten for that client, and why.



Your First 30 Days



Days 1–7 — Absorb. Read the playbook and the editor SOPs. Watch the last year of RDM output — recaps, reels, sessions, testimonials — until you can say how we open, how we pace, and what we consider finished. Set up Resolve to our conventions.



Days 8–14 — Selects and Short-Form. Paper edits, impact statements, B-roll selects, and your first reels through 
 with the Lead Editor reviewing.



Days 15–30 — Long-Form. Your first recap and full session end to end, through QC, to client delivery. Present the Lead Editor a short list of what in our SOPs you would tighten, and why.



Key Responsibilities



Prep: Paper edits from transcripts, impact statements pulled from A-roll, clean B-roll selects timelines.



Long-form: Recaps, full multi-cam sessions, testimonials, and documentary-style pieces — synced, leveled, color-matched, branded.



Short-form: Vertical reels from approved impact statements: hook, B-roll, branding, captions, export.



Technical: Color correction, multi-speaker dialogue matching, brand design language, media management, and timeline sharing.



QC & delivery: Count against scope, watch every second, verify every name, check specs. Revisions upload over the original in 
. Handle every note.



Performance: Review the numbers after posting. Know how each piece did out of ten for that client.



System: ClickUp status against the WBS, Connect Team hours, a daily end-of-day report, and SOP improvements when you find a better way.



What You Bring



2+ years editing professionally, with a reel showing event, interview, or documentary work — not just motion graphics.

DaVinci Resolve proficiency; Resolve Studio preferred. This is our primary NLE and we will not retrain you mid-project.

Story instinct, audio competence, and color fundamentals — including skin tones across a range of complexions.

A real information diet: you watch what performs, and it shows in your work.

A machine and connection that handle 4K workflows, proxies, and large uploads.

Reliable U.S. Eastern overlap, with dependable internet and power and a backup for both.



Who You Are



You are a storyteller who respects a checklist. You can find the moment in a 90-minute keynote and explain why it is the moment, and you can also count to twelve before you hit export. You take direct feedback without flinching and give it the same way. You would rather protect clean capture than rescue it in post, and you already watch what performs before anyone asks you to.



How To Apply



Submit your reel, one full-length piece you cut end to end, a one-paragraph cover letter, and a Loom video (max 5 minutes) breaking down one piece from your reel: its hook, what the middle is doing, and why it ends where it does. Complete the role-specific competency form in the application. 



Competency Form Questions — Video Editor





Name,
, phone number. *

Which role are you applying for? *

What time is 2pm Eastern in your local time zone? *

What hours (Eastern time) are you available Monday–Friday? *

What does Reel Designs Media do, in your own words? *

Which NLE do you work in day to day, and how long have you used DaVinci Resolve specifically? *

Link to your reel, and to one full-length piece — a recap, a session, or a documentary segment — you cut end to end. *

You receive four hours of two-camera keynote footage, a transcript, and a request for a 2-minute recap and six reels. Walk us through your first two hours of work, in order. *

A client returns a revision with fourteen notes, three of which you believe would make the cut worse. What do you do? *

You are about to export and notice the lav audio on the main testimonial has a hum nobody caught on set. Walk us through what you do and who you tell. *

Describe your philosophy as it relates to excellence and accountability. *

What are your full-time salary expectations? *

Please upload your resume. *

title: Lead Generation & Generation Specialist
description:
# Lead Research & Generation Specialist — iMarketU



## About the Role



iMarketU is a digital marketing and automation agency looking for a detail-oriented specialist to research potential clients and organize actionable prospect information in Google Sheets.



We help businesses with websites, lead capture, marketing, and follow-up systems. Your role is to find businesses that could benefit from these services and document why they are a good fit.



## Responsibilities



- Research prospects using targeted keywords, industry terms, and locations.

- Find recent public posts or requests showing buying interest, such as “looking for a web designer,” “need a business website,” or “recommend a marketing agency.”

- Identify other suitable businesses with observable website or marketing gaps, clearly labeling them as cold prospects.

- Find relevant decision-makers and check business contact details against public sources.

- Maintain a clean Google Sheet with consistent formatting, filters, clear statuses, and no duplicates.

- Include the source link, date found, and evidence supporting each prospect’s potential need.

- Provide regular updates on the strongest opportunities.



## Required Google Sheets Information



Business name, industry, location, website, contact name and role, public business
 or phone, relevant social profile, source link, date found, identified need, evidence of interest, lead status, and notes.



Clearly distinguish:

- **Expressed interest:** A business has publicly requested relevant help.

- **Cold prospect:** The business appears suitable, but interest is unconfirmed.

- **Qualified opportunity:** Interest and fit have been confirmed through a conversation.



Do not guess budgets, invent contact information, or label a business interested solely because its website needs improvement.



## Requirements



- Strong online research and keyword-search skills.

- Confidence using Google Sheets.

- Attention to detail and clear written communication.

- Understanding of websites and digital marketing services.

- Ability to prioritize relevant, current opportunities over large contact lists.



This role initially focuses on research and list building. Outreach and appointment setting are separate unless specifically assigned.



## How to Apply



Send a short introduction, relevant experience, availability, and a sample of a lead sheet you have created, with private client information removed.

title: Video Editor — High-End Real Estate Reels
description:
What you'll be editing

Property reels — vertical, under 60 seconds. Cinematic, dynamic, cut to the music. Drone aerials are a core part of every edit, not a filler shot.

Agent brand reels — talking-head format, under 50 seconds. The agent's voice carries the piece, cut around a day-to-night arc with b-roll of the property and the neighborhood.

Listing videos — longer-form walkthroughs for YouTube and listing pages.

Typical raw delivery is 60–70 clips per house, ground and aerial, plus audio where the agent speaks.

What we expect from the edit

Clean rhythm. Cuts land on the track, not near it.

Music-first pacing. A different royalty-free track each video, chosen to fit the property. Music is burned into the export so it clears both Instagram and YouTube.

Modern bold subtitles with a per-video accent color. We specify the color in the brief.

Effects that bookend the piece — one at the open, one at the close, plus motion through the middle. Open-door transitions, speed ramps, subject tracking, tasteful zoom-ins on the agent.

Color that matches the brief. Some edits are soft and filmic, some are sharp and punchy. You adjust.

You pick the strongest takes yourself. We will not timestamp every shot for you.

Requirements

2+ years editing short-form video, ideally real estate, hospitality, luxury, or automotive.

Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, plus After Effects for motion and transitions.

Strong color grading — you can match mixed ground and drone footage into one consistent look.

Comfortable with 
 for delivery and revision notes, and Slack for day-to-day communication.

Reliable written English. You need to read a brief and ask the right question when something is unclear.

Turnaround: first cut within 48 hours of receiving footage. This is our client promise and it does not move. If you cannot commit to that in a given week, you tell us before we send the project, not after.

Nice to have: drone footage experience, sound design instinct (whooshes, risers, ambience), basic photo retouching.

How we work

Footage goes to you through 
 with a written brief: overall direction in a paragraph, then labeled notes on grade, subtitle color, effects, and music options. Revisions are marked directly on the 
 timeline. Everything else happens in Slack.

Project-based to start, paid per video. Volume is steady and growing — editors who consistently deliver on time move to first priority on incoming work and a higher rate.

Rate: [$___ per reel / $___ per listing video] — tell us your rate per finished 60-second vertical reel.

Trial edit

Everyone who makes the shortlist gets the same trial. We send you one real property — ground and aerial footage — with the same written brief our editors get. You deliver one vertical reel under 60 seconds.

Free, one round, no revisions. We are not asking you to work for us for free, we are looking at how you cut.

The trial footage never goes to a client. It is an old project we already delivered.

48 hours, same as a real job, so we both see how the deadline actually feels.

Answer within two days of your delivery. If it lands, you are on the roster and your first paid project goes out that week.

How to apply

2–3 vertical reels you personally cut. Real estate preferred. Links only. Tell us exactly what you did on each if you worked on a team.

Your rate per finished reel and realistic weekly capacity.

Where you source royalty-free music, and one track you would use for a $3M modern home in the Hollywood Hills.

Software you cut on.

title: Part-Time YouTube Shorts Video Editor for Entertainment Channel (Potential to Grow to Full-Time)

title: FULFILMENT AND DISPATCHING SPECIALIST
description:
StressKnotNYC is a therapist-founded mobile massage and wellness company serving clients throughout New York City and surrounding areas. We provide in-home, hotel, workplace, and event massage through a network of licensed massage therapists.

We're hiring an experienced **Fulfillment & Dispatch Specialist** to help run the day-to-day operation behind every session.



Your primary responsibility is making sure **every booking moves successfully from client request → therapist assignment → confirmed session → completed service → post-session follow-up.**



WHAT YOU'LL OWN



1. CLIENT COMMUNICATION

You will be one of the first points of contact for StressKnotNYC clients.



You'll:

* Answer incoming calls, texts, and
s

* Respond quickly and professionally to new inquiries

* Help clients complete bookings

* Answer service and scheduling questions

* Handle appointment changes and client requests

* Keep clients informed while their therapist is being confirmed

* Resolve routine issues and escalate serious concerns appropriately



Clients should never feel like they are chasing us for an answer.



2. FULFILLMENT & DISPATCH

This is the #1 priority of the role.**

When an inquiry call or booking comes in, you are responsible for moving it toward fulfillment.



You'll:

* Review new and upcoming bookings

* Identify the best eligible therapists based on availability, location, service, client preferences, and other requirements

* Contact and dispatch therapists

* Follow up when therapists don't respond

* Find alternatives when the first option isn't available

* Confirm assignments and communicate final details

* Monitor same-day and upcoming sessions

* Handle last-minute changes, delays, cancellations, and coverage issues

* Escalate at-risk bookings early



3. POST-SESSION OPERATIONS

The job doesn't end when the massage ends.



You'll make sure each session is properly closed out by:

* Confirming completion

* Making sure required therapist notes are received

* Reviewing whether any client issue requires attention

* Completing required client follow-up

* Supporting reviews, rebooking, and referrals when appropriate

* Keeping client and session records accurate



4. THERAPIST NETWORK & ONBOARDING

A strong fulfillment operation requires a strong therapist network.



You'll help keep that network growing by:

* Communicating with therapist applicants

* Screening candidates against our requirements

* Scheduling and coordinating interviews

* Following up with qualified candidates

* Collecting required onboarding information and documentation

* Moving approved therapists through onboarding

* Keeping therapist profiles and availability information organized

* Identifying coverage gaps and helping recruit where additional therapists are needed



You're not simply trying to add names to a database. You're helping us maintain a *reliable network of qualified therapists we can confidently send to our clients.*

title: Appointment Setter / Lead Nurturer (UK Hours) — GoHighLevel | Base + Uncapped Commission
description:
Bright Future Digital is a UK digital marketing and lead-generation agency. We're hiring an appointment setter who can;

- Work our leads properly — nurture them, 

- Follow up relentlessly, 

- Book qualified sales calls. Our founder closes; you fill his calendar.



There are three sides to the role: 

1. Book qualified sales calls for our new-client pipeline. You set the appointment, our founder closes it.

2. Make outbound and cold calls to prospect lists we provide or that you source yourself — open the conversation and book the appointment.

3. Call and qualify leads coming into our lead-generation websites, then hand the hot ones over to our clients as premium, ready-to-buy leads.



Day to day, that means:

• Respond to every new lead FAST — within 15 minutes during working hours.

• Make consistent outbound/cold calls to provided and self-sourced prospect lists.

• Follow up persistently across call, SMS,
 and WhatsApp until you get a yes or a clear no.

• Qualify every lead: right decision-maker, genuine need, budget capacity, timeline.

• Book appointments into our calendar, then confirm and remind so people actually show up.

• Keep our GoHighLevel CRM spotless — every lead dispositioned with clear notes.

• Report your numbers to us every week.

What good looks like (the standard your base pays for)

This is a proactive, high-activity seat, not a wait-for-the-phone one. To hold the role you’ll consistently:

• Hit the 15-minute response time on inbound leads during UK hours.

• Make a steady daily volume of outbound dials and structured follow-ups (we’ll agree the number in week one based on the lists — but this is a phone-first role, every day).

• Keep every lead moving through the pipeline with clean, current CRM notes — no lead left untouched.



We track this because our last arrangement failed when leads were left to go cold. Working the leads is the job. Quality beats volume: we cap booked closing calls at a manageable number per week, so your focus is on booking the right meetings that convert, not filling a calendar.



You’re a great fit if you

• Have 2+ years in appointment setting, sales, or outbound.

• Know GoHighLevel well (or a very similar CRM and can learn GHL fast).

• Speak and write excellent English.

• Can work UK business hours (9am–5pm UK time).

• Are organised, genuinely persistent, and understand how lead gen and digital marketing work.

• Have a reliable computer, a good headset, and fast, stable internet.



Compensation (USD) — base plus uncapped commission

We reward closed business, not just a full calendar. The money is weighted toward deals that actually land:

• Base: $500/month, paid bi-weekly, for meeting the daily activity and response standard above.

• + $15 for every appointment that is genuinely qualified and attends. “Qualified” is objective and agreed up front: confirmed decision-maker, stated budget, genuine need, booked and attended — all logged in the CRM.

• + 10% of the first invoice (setup + first month) on every deal that closes, or a flat $150 per close, whichever is higher.

• Uncapped. The more deals you help close, the more you earn — there is no ceiling.



What to realistically expect: 

in a normal month a productive setter earns $300–$800 in commission on top of base — around $800–$1,300 total. The real upside is on closes, so a setter who books well-qualified meetings that convert earns considerably more, and the strongest push toward $1,500+. We won’t quote you an inflated “guaranteed” number — your work rate and the quality of your bookings d
 it, and we’ll be straight with you about volumes from day one.



How this starts — a paid trial with a real gate

The first 30 days is a paid trial on live leads. We’ll agree clear activity and booked-appointment targets in week one. Hit them and you move into the ongoing role with a clear path toward a closing seat and higher commission. It’s a genuine working trial for both of us — we’re building a long-term seat, not filling a gap.



How to apply (read carefully)

1. Send a 2–3 minute audio or Loom recording introducing yourself and telling us about a time you turned a cold or difficult lead into a booked meeting.

2. Tell us which CRMs you’ve used and your experience with GoHighLevel.

3. Start your application with the word “TRADES” so we know you read this properly. Applications without it are deleted.

We reply to every serious applicant.

title: Marketing Technology & Automation Specialist
description:
# Marketing Technology & Automation Specialist



### GoHighLevel | AI | Automation | Websites | SEO | Content



**Location:** Philippines — Remote

**Position:** Full-Time

**Schedule:** Must have meaningful overlap with U.S. Central Time



We are looking for a highly resourceful Marketing Technology & Automation Specialist to support multiple growing U.S.-based service businesses.



This is **not just a GoHighLevel position.**



We need someone who can become the technical person behind the scenes who makes things work.



You may be building a GHL workflow in the morning, troubleshooting an integration later that day, updating a website, fixing an indexing problem, helping launch a Meta campaign, setting up an AI automation, or turning a long-form podcast into short-form content.



You don't have to be the world's best expert in every one of these areas.



You **do** need to be technically strong, extremely resourceful, willing to learn, and able to take ownership of projects without needing someone to constantly follow up with you.



## Your Core Responsibilities



You will help manage and improve:



**GoHighLevel**



* CRM setup and maintenance

* Workflows and automations

* Pipelines

* Funnels and landing pages

* Forms and surveys

* Calendars

*
 and SMS campaigns

* Lead nurture systems

* Database reactivation

* Reputation management

* GHL AI tools

* Subaccounts and snapshots

* Reporting and troubleshooting



**Automation & Integrations**



* Zapier

* Make

* Webhooks and APIs

* Meta/Facebook lead 

* Google integrations

* Calendar integrations

* Forms and lead routing

* Troubleshooting failed automations and integrations



**Websites & Funnels**



* GHL and/or WordPress

* Landing pages

* Website updates

* Forms

* Domain/DNS management

* Mobile optimization

* Tracking pixels

* Google Analytics

* Google Tag Manager

* Google Search Console



**SEO**



* On-page SEO

* Technical SEO

* Local SEO

* Keyword research

* Google Business Profile

* Search Console

* Indexing

* Service and location pages

* Basic SEO reporting



**AI & Technology**



* ChatGPT, Claude, or similar AI platforms

* AI-assisted workflows

* AI agents and automations

* Content generation and repurposing

* Researching and implementing new technology when it can actually improve the business



**Content & Video**



* Turn long-form videos and podcasts into short clips

* YouTube Shorts

*
/Instagram Reels

* Captions and subtitles

* Basic thumbnails and graphics

* Canva, CapCut, Descript, or similar tools

* Uploading, formatting and scheduling content



**Paid Marketing Support**



* Meta/Facebook Ads

* YouTube/Google Ads

* Lead forms

* Pixels and conversion tracking

* Retargeting

* Audiences

* Basic campaign setup and reporting



## What Matters Most



Technical ability matters.



**Execution matters more.**



We are specifically looking for someone who:



* Finishes projects.

* Meets deadlines.

* Communicates without being chased.

* Gives clear beginning-of-day and end-of-day updates.

* Works priorities one at a time through completion.

* Tests their work before saying it is finished.

* Identifies problems proactively.

* Researches solutions independently.

* Asks questions when necessary instead of sitting stuck.

* Documents systems so someone else can understand them.

* Can manage their own workload and commitments.

* Tells us BEFORE a deadline when there is a problem — not after the deadline passes.



If you need someone constantly asking:



**“Is this done yet?”**



this position is probably not for you.



We don't expect perfection.



We **do** expect ownership.



## Who We Are



You will initially support two businesses:



**Uptown Window cleaning** a window cleaning and pressure washing company



**BBV — Building Better Business Ventures** — a growing business platform helping service-business owners with staffing, marketing, automation, systems and business growth.



This means the systems you build won't simply be internal projects. As BBV grows, many of these systems may ultimately be deployed across client businesses.



We therefore care about building things **cleanly, repeatably and correctly.**



## What We Want to See When You Apply



Please send:



1. A short introduction about yourself.

2. Your years of GoHighLevel experience.

3. Examples/screenshots or Loom videos of GHL systems you personally built.

4. Websites or funnels you personally built.

5. Examples of automations or integrations you created.

6. SEO work you've performed and the results.

7. Examples of video/content work you've produced.

8. Your experience with Meta, Google or YouTube advertising.

9. The AI tools you currently use and how you use them.

10. Your expected monthly compensation in PHP/USD.



### And answer these three questions:



**1. Tell us about a technical problem you didn't know how to solve when it was assigned to you. How did you figure it out?**



**2. Tell us about a project where you were going to miss a deadline. When did you tell your manager, and what did you do about it?**



**3. You are given five projects Monday morning, but realistically you can only finish three by Friday. What do you do?**



Please do not use AI to give us the answer you think we want.



We would rather hear an imperfect answer from you than a perfect answer from ChatGPT.



## Hiring Process



Qualified applicants will complete:



**Step 1:** Application review

**Step 2:** Technical interview

**Step 3:** Practical skills test

**Step 4:** Final interview



The practical test will involve completing real-world GHL/automation tasks so we can evaluate how you think, build, troubleshoot, communicate and finish work.



We're looking for someone who can become a long-term technical member of our team — not simply someone waiting for their next freelance project.
